meaning: Which conventional kunya, followed in the text by the honorific marker, names which Imam in an Imami chain. Owner decision 2026-11-21: such a mention identifies that Imam and counts toward the machine-reviewed tier; every other kunya-only name stays a label. Reviewable data, not a scholarly claim: edit this file to change the rule, then rebuild the projection.

applies_to.works: every Imami work in the archive; all were compiled after the eleventh Imam, so no period restriction separates the Imams who share a kunya
applies_to.never: Sunni, Ibadi and Zaydi chains (an Imami convention; a kunya-only name there stays a label)

marker.where: at the end of the written surface, or immediately after the name in the report's own Arabic

rule: A surface that is exactly a kunya below, optionally followed by one listed qualifier, with the marker. Unshared kunya, or a qualifier naming one Imam: that Imam (basis imam_kunya_convention). A kunya shared by several Imams with no qualifier: a labelled candidate for each listed Imam (basis imam_kunya_candidate), never the machine-reviewed tier. Any other words after the kunya (al-Barqi, al-Ahwal, al-ʿAbdi ...): not an Imam, nothing is emitted.

kunyas.why_unqualified: Owner's example (2026-11-21): in Imami chains a bare Abu ʿAbd Allah with the marker is al-Sadiq; al-Husayn is written with his name.
Shared by al-Baqir and al-Jawad (Abu Jaʿfar al-Thani), both cited bare in al-Kafi; owner question whether bare means al-Baqir by convention.
Shared by al-Kazim (al-Awwal), al-Rida (al-Thani) and al-Hadi (al-Thalith).
The conventional kunya of al-Kazim in Imami chains.
Shared by al-Hasan al-Mujtaba, ʿAli ibn al-Husayn and al-Hasan al-ʿAskari.
